This feature, updated daily, tracks notable capital allocation decisions across the travel industry, following where the next dollar is going.

Skift Intelligence is built on a framework designed to track every decision that determines where the next dollar in travel is going. Capital Moves, a new feature updated daily, tracks every notable capital allocation announcement across global travel.

Hotels and aviation accounted for 37 of the 59 capital moves Skift tracked in October, and they tell two different stories.

In hotels, money changed hands, and sellers recycled capital or worked through distress. Pandox sold seven Nordic hotels to pay down debt, receivers sold two Shimao hotels in Hong Kong, and two Indian hotels passed to a new owner through insolvency. Buyers consolidated, from Endeavor’s seven-hotel portfolio around Chicago Midway Airport to Sunday PropTech’s deal for Fletcher’s roughly 170 hotels.

In aviation, money went into future capacity and the debt to fund it. Avolon ordered 250 aircraft and Aviation Capital Group 75 more, while Southwest, IndiGo and Allegiant lined up financing.

Startup funding stayed modest. Ten of the 17 venture financings were $5 million or less. The AI money that did move went mostly into plumbing: connecting AI agents to travel inventory, automating hotel guest messaging and tracking hotel prices
